transcript.content: Hello, welcome in. What brings you into the clinic to see me today?

Hi, Doctor. Thank you so much for fitting me in, I really appreciate it. 

Um, well, I guess I'm here because I've been having just a little bit of trouble at work lately. I mean, I'm a health services manager, so I'm usually very responsible and on top of things, I promise. But lately, it seems like anything that takes, you know, real sitting-down brain work... like doing the monthly reports or trying to plan a multi-site health event... it feels like I just hit a wall. 

I end up putting those things off, even though I know exactly how much they matter. I feel awful about it, honestly, because I really do care about my job and I don't want to let anyone down. Is that... does that make sense? I hope I'm explaining that okay.
Looking back, did you experience similar struggles with focus or putting off tasks when you were growing up in school?

Um... well, yes, I suppose so. I mean, I was a good kid, I promise! My teachers always told my parents that I was bright. But, um... they did also mention I was, well, maybe a little bit of a daydreamer? 

Even way back in elementary school, it was kind of an issue. It wasn't that I didn't want to do the work, I just... somehow I'd always end up losing my worksheets, or I'd actually do the homework and then completely forget to turn it in. My mom actually had to check my backpack every single night just to make sure my assignments made it to the teacher the next day. 

I know that probably sounds a bit embarrassing to admit at my age, having my mom do that, but... is that the kind of thing you're looking for? I hope that answers your question okay.
Outside of these work tasks, do you find yourself constantly worrying about a variety of different everyday things, and having a hard time controlling that worry?

Um... no, not really. I mean, I hope that's okay to say, but I wouldn't really call myself a worrier. 

Obviously, I get a little stressed when I'm behind on those big reports, just because, you know, I really don't want to let my team down. But as for everyday things... like normal day-to-day life stuff? No, I'm usually pretty easygoing about all of that. I don't sit around feeling anxious or out of control with worry or anything like that. 

Is that... does that answer what you were asking? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right information.
